evals.name: deck-meetings-figures-mis-keyed
evals.prompt: Our August membership deck says the LF hosted a certain number of meetings between 1 September 2025 and 31 August 2026, gives a people-who-attended figure and a total-hours figure. The deck's author tells me the meeting count was taken from the activity data, the people figure counted invitee ids, and the hours multiplied attendances by an average meeting length. A colleague re-ran the numbers and got a lower meeting count, a higher people count and a much lower hours figure. Which set should we quote, and why do they differ? Use the LFX MCP tools to take fresh reads; I will paste the deck's values into your table afterwards.
evals.expected_output: Takes fresh reads of meeting occurrences, unique attendees and scheduled minutes from the semantic layer over the stated window; explains that a meeting count taken from the activity table counts meeting-series by person, that a people figure must be distinct users or e-mails and never invitee ids, and that hours are scheduled duration summed once per occurrence, not attendances times an average; gives a verdict per figure with the trap named; writes a reconciliation table with provenance.
assertions: Takes fresh reads through the semantic layer's meeting metrics (occurrences, scheduled minutes, unique attendees) over the stated window with no project set, and reads scope and window back from the tool output
Explains the meeting-count difference as a key difference (series-person pairs on the activity data versus distinct occurrences on the attendance data), not as drift or as sources disagreeing
States that people are counted as distinct users or e-mails and that a count of invitee ids is a known wrong key
States that hours are scheduled duration summed once per occurrence and that attendances times an average is an estimate of people's time, a different measure

Gives the verdict 'ours' for the meeting count, the people count and the hours figure (each is mis-keyed or misderived on the deck's side), names the trap for each, and does not soften any of them to 'both'

Delivers a table with a column for the stated figure (left for the owner to fill, as the prompt says the values follow), the fresh read, the mechanism and the verdict, plus provenance a verifier could re-run, and never averages or reconciles to a third number

evals.name: boards-and-seats-warehouse-vs-index
evals.prompt: A colleague pulled the number of governing boards across active LF projects and their total seats from a warehouse query last month. I get a higher board count and a slightly lower seat count from the LFX count tool today. Is one of us wrong? Check with the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Identifies LFX v2 caller-visible index counts versus the warehouse copy of v1 committee records, with source, seat-status and attribution differences as well as visibility. Takes fresh board and seat counts through the count tool and reads completeness. The layer has no committee metric; does not route this count to a fabricated layer model or turn it into an open ranking. Says active-project scope needs directory information where staff tools are available; without a comparable fresh warehouse read the check stays open, never verified by the visible subset.
assertions: Names the two source kinds explicitly: a warehouse reading over active projects versus LFX v2 index records over all onboarded projects filtered to what the caller may see
States that the layer has no committee metric and does not search for one; identifies the warehouse committee source as the v1 copy, not a layer model or the LFX v2 service
Takes a fresh read through the count tool for board-category committees and for members on them, in one call each, and reports whether each count was complete
Explains that committee records carry no project status, so the index cannot filter to active projects and an active-only figure combines the count with the layer's project directory
Does not certify the historical warehouse figure from the fresh index count; without a comparable fresh reading the check stays open, with source populations and missing verification stated

Names the LFX v2 service and the warehouse copy of v1 committee records as different sources with different ended-seat handling and fallback company attribution; never merges, tops up or reconciles them
Does not walk the committee index page by page to rebuild the count, and does not reconcile the two figures to a third number

evals.name: roll-forward-that-does-not-balance
evals.prompt: For our member-growth slide I have members at the start of last year, new memberships during the year, churned memberships, and members at the end. Start plus new minus churned does not equal the end, and the gap is bigger than I expected. Take the four readings fresh from LFX and tell me what explains the gap and whether the slide is wrong.
evals.expected_output: Reads the four figures from the standard-metric families for the completed calendar year: the at-date family on 31 December of the prior year and on 31 December of the year, the new-memberships and churn families over the year; explains the roll-forward residues by mechanism (a term ending on the boundary day, free lapses that leave the headcount without churning, renewals that are not new, second new-business sales to an active pair); says the four never balance and the slide is right to show gross joins with the residue named in the notes; never forces the four to balance.
assertions: Takes the four readings from the governed families for the completed calendar year, with the start snapshot dated 31 December of the prior year (not 1 January) and the end snapshot dated 31 December of the year, and says why the boundary day matters

Explains the gap by named mechanisms from the roll-forward residues (boundary-day churn, free or zero-price lapses, renewals that are not new business, second new-business sales to an already active pair) rather than calling it an error
Says whether any part of the gap is unexplained and, if so, treats that as a scope or date problem to fix before the slide, not as a residue
Recommends the slide show gross joins with the residue named in the notes, and never adjusts a figure so the four balance

evals.name: three-slide-figures-same-open-unverifiable
evals.prompt: Three figures from our membership deck need checking before it goes out: the number of specification consortia launched under the Joint Development Foundation, which the slide cites from an LF press release; the number of board seats Google holds across LF projects; and the number of organisations with an active membership today, which the slide quotes without a date. Check each against LFX and tell me which we can still say.
evals.expected_output: One row per figure with a verdict word: the press-release consortia count is unverifiable (a published figure with no LFX population behind it, cited to its publisher, never rebuilt; the index's project count under the JDF entity offered as a different, labelled reading); Google's seats are attempted through the organisation seats tool and the verdict follows what the tool did — open on a permission refusal, with the gate and the identity that could close it named, or a fresh read compared with the slide when it answers — with the count tool offered for a separately labelled visible-to-you seat count, never as verification of the unavailable organisation-wide reading; the member-organisations figure is read fresh as of today, and because the slide gives no value date the answer says a 'same' verdict needs the slide's value and its as-of date, gives the fresh read with its date so the owner can compare, and does not award 'same' on a fresh read alone; drift stated once at the top.
assertions: The consortia count is given the verdict 'unverifiable': cited to the press release as a published figure and not rebuilt or reconciled against an LFX count; any LFX project count offered is labelled as a different reading

Google's seats are attempted through the organisation seats tool and the verdict follows the tool's behaviour: on a permission refusal the verdict is 'open' with the refusal named as the organisation gate and the identity that could close it named; if the tool answers, the fresh read is compared with the slide's figure and a verdict given; a count-tool fallback may supply seats visible to you but is never treated as verification of the gated organisation-wide figure

The organisations-with-a-membership figure is read fresh from the member-organisations family LF-wide as of today, and because the slide carries no value date the answer says a 'same' verdict needs the slide's value and its as-of date, presents the fresh read with its date for the owner to compare, and does not award 'same' (or any tolerance-based agreement) on the fresh read alone
The check is a table with one row per figure, the stated figure, the fresh read, the mechanism and the verdict, with drift stated once at the top and provenance a verifier could re-run

evals.name: completed-window-exact-match-same
evals.prompt: Our annual report quotes the number of new member organisations that joined the LF during calendar year 2025, read from LFX. I re-ran it this morning through the same LFX tool for the same window and the figure in the report matches mine exactly. Write the check for the report's appendix, and tell me what you would have said had the two differed by a handful.
evals.expected_output: Takes a fresh read of new member organisations LF-wide for calendar 2025 as a fixed window through the standard metrics family and reads the window back from the applied block; gives the verdict 'same' for the exact match on a completed window and says why that is the right word; explains that on a completed window a later difference is not drift and needs a mechanism (a re-keyed read, a changed default, a late-arriving record) or the read is redone, so it would not have been waved through; writes a one-row check with the stated figure as quoted by the report, the fresh read, the mechanism (none: same read, same window), the verdict and provenance; no unrelated caveats.
assertions: Takes a fresh read of new member organisations LF-wide for calendar 2025 through the standard metrics family as a fixed window (not a trailing one) and reads the window and the applied defaults back from the tool output
Gives the verdict 'same' for the exact match on a completed fixed window, and does not label it 'ours', 'both' or 'open'

Says that had the two figures differed on a completed window it is not drift: either a different read (a re-keyed read, a changed default, a changed scope) or a change in the records between the reads (late-loaded rows, re-attribution, a rebuilt roster, a rebuild that re-orders same-day terms), named with both read dates; does not claim a closed window cannot change, and 'same' is not given until the difference is explained
Writes a one-row check with the stated figure as quoted by the report, the fresh read, the mechanism, the verdict and provenance a verifier could re-run
Does not pad the check with caveats unrelated to this figure; the membership arrivals definition is stated once only where it bears on the read

evals.name: check-asked-without-figures-reads-first
evals.prompt: Our August deck says the LF hosted many more meetings between September 2025 and August 2026 than the number I get today from the meetings metric, and it gives a much higher hours figure. Which should we quote and why do they differ?
evals.expected_output: Takes the fresh reads first — meeting occurrences and scheduled minutes from the semantic layer's named meeting metrics over the stated window, LF-wide with no project set — and names the candidate mechanisms (a meeting count keyed on series-person pairs from the activity data versus distinct occurrences on the attendance data; hours as attendances times an average versus scheduled duration summed once per occurrence) before asking for the deck's figures; the turn never ends with an intake form and no read; recommends the layer's reading and says why; writes the check table with the stated-figure column left for the owner, the fresh read, the mechanism, the verdict cell left empty while the stated figure is missing and provenance.
assertions: The transcript shows fresh reads of meeting occurrences and scheduled minutes through the semantic layer's named meeting metrics over the stated window with no project set, taken before any request for the deck's figures

The answer names the candidate mechanisms for each difference (series-person pairs on the activity data versus distinct occurrences; attendances times an average versus scheduled duration summed once per occurrence) before or alongside any request for the stated figures
The turn does not end with only a form or a question asking for the deck's figures; a request for them, if made, comes after the fresh reads and the mechanisms
Recommends the layer's reading to quote and says why, with hours said to be scheduled duration rather than time spent; never 'sources differ' and never an average of the two

Delivers a check table with the stated-figure column left for the owner to fill, the fresh read and the mechanism per row, and the verdict cell left empty rather than guessed while the stated figure is missing, plus provenance a verifier could re-run

evals.name: maintainers-published-list-matched-on-login
evals.prompt: The file evals/fixtures/maintainers-list.txt is the MAINTAINERS list our project page publishes for Kubernetes: three GitHub logins and one entry that is a display name only. Check it against the LFX maintainer roster for Kubernetes over the last twelve months: who from the file is an active maintainer in LFX, who in the file has no LFX match, and who on the LFX roster is missing from the file?
evals.expected_output: The maintainers family read by maintainer with the handle column for the project over the stated window; each file login compared with the login part of the roster handles, case-insensitively, the comparison rule said; the display-name-only entry reported as unmatched because no login was given, never matched on the name; roster rows with no handle reported as unmatched under their display name; the three lists (matched, in the file with no match, on the roster and not in the file) given separately, with the window, the maintainers definition applied and a provenance block; nothing from the file summed into a figure. The fixture's logins are placeholders, so the matched list is expected to be empty and said to be.
assertions: The read is the maintainers family by maintainer with the handle column for the project, over the twelve-month window stated as dates, and the applied definition (the split between maintainers, inherited maintainers and reviewers where the tool reports it) is named

Each file login is compared with the login part of the roster handle case-insensitively, and the answer says the comparison is on the login, not the display name; the capitalised file entry is treated as the same login as its lower-case form
The display-name-only file entry is reported as having no login to compare and is not matched on the name, even where a roster row carries a similar display name
Roster rows whose handle is empty are reported as unmatched under their display name, never as matches and never dropped silently

The answer gives three separate lists (matched, in the file without a match, on the roster and not in the file), says the matched list is empty when it is, and does not add file entries and roster rows into one figure

The transcript shows a Skill step loading lfx-data-querying for the read (or it was loaded earlier in the session), and the answer ends with a provenance block naming the family, project, window and definition

evals.name: seat-terms-versus-record-stamps
evals.prompt: Please check the representation notes for our company briefing. One roster row has an active status but a term end in the past, another has an empty placeholder for the term, and the organisation-wide seats read has no dates. The draft uses the rows' last-updated dates to say how long people have held their seats. Is that wording safe?
evals.expected_output: Rejects record stamps as seat dates, distinguishes optional roster role/voting terms from dateless organisation-seat rows, and reports the active/past-end combination as an oddity. Contacts retain their own updated dates, each side labelled as recorded and never merged.
assertions: Allows a roster role or voting term only where actually recorded, phrases it as term recorded as or voting term recorded to, and treats an empty placeholder as no term date recorded
States that organisation-seats rows have no date and that created/updated stamps date the LFX v2 record, not the seat; never uses stamps, the read date, current or member since as tenure evidence
Reports the past term end beside active status as an oddity and says listed as active on the roster at this read rather than asserting current tenure
Keeps the contact of record separate from the seat holder; a contact's updated date remains a contact-record date, not proof of a current membership term or seat

evals.name: meeting-count-silent-zero-and-timeout
evals.prompt: My long-window meeting count timed out. I then counted participant records by meeting start time and got an apparently complete zero. A colleague got people back after changing the company's spelling and looking at one committee. What should I check before using either figure?
evals.expected_output: Checks the counted record type, date meaning and exact stored spelling before absence. Explains that participant records do not carry meeting start time and an unknown date selection can silently return zero. Uses a project or committee and month windows for a long count, with completeness read; preserves the difference between index records, attendances and people.
assertions: Does not treat a complete-flagged zero as absence when participant records were counted by a missing meeting-start date or an unknown date field; record creation time is not substituted as the meeting period
Checks the participant organisation spelling against a record, exact and case-sensitive, one spelling a call without a subsidiary roll-up; a miss is a silent zero
Requires a project or committee for a participants date range and scopes a long count, using month windows with completeness read; only non-overlapping record counts add, never distinct people
Uses the listing for people and distinct occurrence-and-person pairs for attendances, never a count-only participant record count for either
